react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment) converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP ORA returns KEGG:map00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 (Galactose Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00182 (Galactosemia) both at FDR = 1.06×10⁻¹³ with five overlapping input metabolites: sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, galactinol, and galactitol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 as its single top hit (p = 5.16×10⁻⁸, raw p-value), matching the identical five metabolites within a 27-compound KEGG pathway roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis places galactose metabolism at rank 4 (p = 0.0075) with 12 of 13 pathway members hit — the highest overlap ratio of any Mummichog hit — confirming the signal is robust even under mass-based network propagation. The five driver metabolites all belong to the Leloir pathway and its downstream sugar-alcohol branch: sucrose feeds the pathway upstream, galactinol (the galactosyl donor for raffinose-family oligosaccharide synthesis) is a Leloir intermediate, galactitol is the aldose-reductase product of galactose, and myo-inositol and glycerol serve as the inositol-phosphatidylinositol and glycerol-phosphate backbone donors for glycolipid and glycerophospholipid biosynthesis that branch from galactose catabolism. Farnesyl pyrophosphate, ureidosuccinic acid, D-glucose, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, acetaminophen, and aspirin do not map to the galactose network in any paradigm, consistent with the treatment selectively perturbing the Leloir flux rather than general sugar metabolism. The galactosemia disease module (SMPDB:SMP00182) achieves the same extreme significance as the canonical pathway, suggesting the treatment may model a mild galactosemia-like metabolic state.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA returns SMPDB:SMP00043 (Galactose Metabolism) at rank 1 with FDR = 1.06×10⁻¹³ and fold-enrichment = 1089.5, matching KEGG:map00052 at the same score (rank 2). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 (Galactose Metabolism) as its single top hit at p = 5.16×10⁻⁸ with 5 overlapping input compounds out of 27 pathway members. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis hits MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 (p = 0.0079) with 12 of 13 pathway members matched, providing near-complete coverage under mass-based network propagation. The five driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116), all confirmed as pathway members in SMPDB:SMP00043, KEGG:hsa00052, and MUMM:galactose_metabolism. Sucrose drives the pathway by supplying glucose for entry into the Leloir pathway arm, while GALK (EC 2.7.1.6) catalyzes the phosphorylation of D-galactose to D-galactose-1-phosphate as the first committed step. Glycerol (KEGG:C00116) is a confirmed member of KEGG:hsa00052, and myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137) is confirmed as a member of KEGG:hsa00052.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment) converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP ORA returns KEGG:map00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043 (Galactose Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00182 (Galactosemia) both at FDR = 1.06×10⁻¹³ with five overlapping input metabolites: sucrose, myo-inositol, glycerol, galactinol, and galactitol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 as its single top hit (p = 5.16×10⁻⁸, raw p-value), matching the identical five metabolites within a 27-compound KEGG pathway roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis places galactose metabolism at rank 4 (p = 0.0075) with 12 of 13 pathway members hit — the highest overlap ratio of any Mummichog hit — confirming the signal is robust even under mass-based network propagation. The five driver metabolites all belong to the Leloir pathway and its downstream sugar-alcohol branch: sucrose feeds the pathway upstream, galactinol (the galactosyl donor for raffinose-family oligosaccharide synthesis) is a Leloir intermediate, galactitol is the aldose-reductase product of galactose, and myo-inositol and glycerol serve as the inositol-phosphatidylinositol and glycerol-phosphate backbone donors for glycolipid and glycerophospholipid biosynthesis that branch from galactose catabolism. Farnesyl pyrophosphate, ureidosuccinic acid, D-glucose, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, acetaminophen, and aspirin do not map to the galactose network in any paradigm, consistent with the treatment selectively perturbing the Leloir flux rather than general sugar metabolism. The galactosemia disease module (SMPDB:SMP00182) achieves the same extreme significance as the canonical pathway, suggesting the treatment may model a mild galactosemia-like metabolic state.
